question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution:
The correct answer is '**catalysed**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase “The invention of the Internet, in particular,” is followed by a verb that describes a completed action in the past.
 
• The simple past tense is appropriate here as the sentence refers to a specific past event (the invention of the Internet).
 
• “Catalysed” is the simple past form of the verb “catalyse” and fits correctly in this context.
 
• Other options like “catalyse” (base form), “catalyses” (present simple), and “catalysing” (present participle) do not align with the past tense context.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The evolution of technology has **led__** to unprecedented advancements in various fields, from medicine to communication. The invention of the Internet, in particular, (2) **__catalysed__** a global revolution, altering how people connect and share information. Innovations in artificial intelligence and machine learning (3) **_________****automation and efficiency, transforming industries and creating new economic paradigms. As technology (4) **_________****to evolve, ethical and social implications (5) **_________****significant consideration.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Catalysed – Past tense; means caused or accelerated a reaction or change, which is contextually correct.
 
• Catalyse – Base form; not used in a past context without auxiliary verbs.
 
• Catalyses – Present tense; incorrect since the sentence refers to a past event.
 
• Catalysing – Present participle; incorrect in this grammatical structure.
